s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive unilateral skin hardening with limited joint motion and associated skin changes
salient_findings: Unilateral skin hardening on the right thigh and buttock
Mild hypertrichosis and hyperpigmentation of the affected skin
Limited motion of the right limb joint
key_facts: 11-year-old boy presented with a 7-year history of progressive skin hardening
Skin hardening is unilateral and involves the right thigh and buttock
Recent limitation of motion in the right limb joint
Normal results for routine blood tests, autoantibodies, immunoglobulins, C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
MRI of the right thigh showed slight thickening of subcutaneous tissue and T2 signal abnormality
Histopathological findings included normal epidermis, mild pigmentation, and increased density of fibroblasts
Immunohistochemical staining showed increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis
Alcian blue staining was negative

shortlist.label: Linear Scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Unilateral skin hardening with joint limitation and characteristic histopathological findings

shortlist.label: Morphea
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive skin hardening with increased density of fibroblasts and normal epidermis

shortlist.label: Scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Skin hardening with limited joint motion, although less likely due to unilateral presentation

shortlist.label: Stiff Skin Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by stony-hard skin with loss of elasticity, matching the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Lipodermatosclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Skin hardening and hyperpigmentation, although the patient's age and lack of venous insufficiency make it less likely
